arxiv-2203-07290.title: GradTac: Spatio-Temporal Gradient Based Tactile Sensing Thanks: All authors are associated with the Perception and Robotics Group, University of Maryland, College Park, MD, 20740. Thanks: {kganguly, mppavan, cmparam9, fermulcm, nitinsan, jyaloimo}@umd.edu
arxiv-2203-07290.creator: Kanishka Ganguly, Pavan Mantripragada, Chethan M. Parameshwara
arxiv-2203-07290.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Kanishka Ganguly, Pavan Mantripragada, Chethan M. Parameshwara. Tactile sensing for robotics is achieved through a variety of mechanisms, including magnetic, optical-tactile, and conductive fluid. Currently, the fluid-based sensors have struck the right balance of anthropomorphic sizes and shapes and accuracy of tactile response measurement. However, this design is plagued by a low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR) due to the fluid based sensing mechanism “damping” the measurement values that are hard to model.

This work of the second author was funded by the
arxiv-2301-05448.creator: Yuming Ba, Dean S. Oliver
arxiv-2301-05448.description: Abstract The weighting of critical-point samples in the weighted randomized maximum likelihood method depend on the magnitude of the data mismatch at the critical points and on the Jacobian of the transformation from the prior density to the proposal density. When standard iterative ensemble smoothers are applied for data assimilation, the Jacobian is identical for all samples.

arxiv-2301-11845.title: Learning the Effects of Physical Actions in a Multi-modal Environment
arxiv-2301-11845.creator: Gautier Dagan, Frank Keller, Alex Lascarides
arxiv-2301-11845.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) handle physical commonsense information inadequately. As a result of being trained in a disembodied setting, LLMs often fail to predict an action’s outcome in a given environment. However, predicting the effects of an action before it is executed is crucial in planning, where coherent sequences of actions are often needed to achieve a goal.

arxiv-2405-13462.title: Blockchain and Artificial Intelligence: Synergies and Conflicts
arxiv-2405-13462.creator: Leon Witt, Armando Teles Fortes, Kentaroh Toyoda, Member , IEEE, Wojciech Samek, Member , IEEE, Dan Li, Member , IEEE
arxiv-2405-13462.description: Abstract Blockchain technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) have emerged as transformative forces in their respective domains. This paper explores synergies and challenges between these two technologies. Our research analyses the biggest projects combining blockchain and AI, based on market capitalization, and derives a novel framework to categorize contemporary and future use cases.

arxiv-2407-18898.title: A Flexible and Scalable Approach for Collecting Wildlife Advertisements on the Web
arxiv-2407-18898.creator: Juliana Barbosa, Sunandan Chakraborty, Juliana Freire
arxiv-2407-18898.description: Abstract Wildlife traffickers are increasingly carrying out their activities in cyberspace. As they advertise and sell wildlife products in online marketplaces, they leave digital traces of their activity. This creates a new opportunity: by analyzing these traces, we can obtain insights into how trafficking networks work as well as how they can be disrupted. However, collecting such information is difficult.

arxiv-2501-18673.title: Length scale estimation of excited quantum oscillators
arxiv-2501-18673.creator: Tyler Volkoff, Giri Gopalan
arxiv-2501-18673.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tyler Volkoff, Giri Gopalan. Massive quantum oscillators are finding increasing applications in proposals for high-precision quantum sensors and interferometric detection of weak forces. Although optimal estimation of certain properties of massive quantum oscillators such as phase shifts and displacements have strict counterparts in the theory of quantum estimation of the electromagnetic field, the phase space anisotropy of the massive oscillator is characterized by a length scale parameter that is an independent target for quantum estimation methods.

arxiv-2502-16830.title: Dynamic Basis Function Generation for Network Revenue Management
arxiv-2502-16830.creator: Daniel Adelman, Christiane Barz, Alba V. Olivares-Nadal
arxiv-2502-16830.description: Abstract This paper introduces an algorithm that dynamically generates basis functions to approximate the value function in Network Revenue Management. Unlike existing algorithms sampling the parameters of new basis functions, this Nonlinear Incremental Algorithm (NLIAlg) iteratively refines the value function approximation by optimizing these parameters.

arxiv-2507-22371.title: SAEL: Leveraging Large Language Models with Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts for Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection Thanks: 1 Lei Yu and Shiqi Cheng contributed equally to this work. Thanks: ∗ Corresponding authors: Li Yang and Fengjun Zhang.
arxiv-2507-22371.creator: Lei Yu 2 3 1 , Shiqi Cheng 2 1 , Zhirong Huang 2 3 , Jingyuan Zhang 2 3 , Chenjie Shen 2 3 , Junyi Lu 2 3 , Li Yang 2 ∗ \ast , Fengjun Zhang 2 4 ∗ \ast , Jiajia Ma 2
arxiv-2507-22371.description: Abstract With the increasing security issues in blockchain, smart contract vulnerability detection has become a research focus. Existing vulnerability detection methods have their limitations: 1) Static analysis methods struggle with complex scenarios. 2) Methods based on specialized pre-trained models perform well on specific datasets but have limited generalization capabilities.

arxiv-2510-09000.title: When inverse seesaw meets inverse electroweak phase transition: a novel path to leptogenesis
arxiv-2510-09000.creator: Wen-Yuan Ai, Peisi Huang, and Ke-Pan Xie
arxiv-2510-09000.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Wen-Yuan Ai, Peisi Huang, and Ke-Pan Xie. We propose a new nonthermal leptogenesis mechanism triggered by the cosmic first-order phase transition. The Standard Model is extended with two generations of TeV-scale vectorlike leptons. The lighter generation gives rise to an inverse electroweak phase transition of the Higgs field at T ∼ 200 ​ GeV T\sim 200~{\rm GeV} , restoring the symmetry, and resulting in relativistic bubble expansion in the space. The heavier generation is responsible for neutrino masses via the inverse seesaw mechanism.

arxiv-2510-25936.title: Reading Radio from Camera: Visually-Grounded, Lightweight, and Interpretable RSSI Prediction
arxiv-2510-25936.creator: Sen Yan, Tianyu Hu, Brahim Mefgouda, Samson Lasaulce and Merouane Debbah
arxiv-2510-25936.description: Abstract Accurate, real-time wireless signal prediction is essential for next-generation networks. However, existing vision-based frameworks often rely on computationally intensive models and are also sensitive to environmental interference. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel, physics-guided and light-weighted framework that predicts the received signal strength indicator (RSSI) from camera images.

pmc-13367633.title: Exploring Faculty Development Initiatives at Avalon University School of Medicine: A Case Study
pmc-13367633.creator: Sateesh B Arja, Praveen Kottath Veetil, Simi Paramban, Ibrahim Ibikunle, Mohamed Fakhry Abedelbaky, Sireesha Bala Arja
pmc-13367633.description: IntroductionAs medical education shifts toward competency-based curricula, faculty must navigate evolving expectations for teaching, mentoring, assessment, and scholarship. Despite their central role in training future health professionals, medical educators often face ambiguity regarding career advancement through teaching. Promotion criteria in academic institutions are frequently research-focused, leaving faculty unclear about how to document and demonstrate teaching excellence and educational innovation.
